questions.q: What buckets does northfield-glue-role have access to?
options: Only northfield-raw-zone, northfield-curated-zone, and northfield-glue-scripts
Every bucket in the AWS account
Only northfield-curated-zone, read-only
No S3 access — it only needs Glue Catalog permissions
questions.explain: The role used by the crawler and ETL job is scoped to exactly the three buckets the pipeline actually touches, nothing account-wide.

questions.q: Why does northfield-stepfunctions-role name the exact ARN of northfield-orders-etl instead of granting glue:StartJobRun on Resource: '*'?
options: So the role can only ever start this one specific Glue job, even if the account later gains other Glue jobs it shouldn't touch
Because Resource: '*' is technically invalid JSON in IAM policies
Exact ARNs make the policy load faster
There is no difference in effect between the two approaches
questions.explain: Resource-level scoping to a specific ARN prevents the role from silently gaining power over future, unrelated resources in the account.

options: Read-only access (s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket) to northfield-curated-zone only
Full read/write access to both the raw and curated zones
Write access to northfield-raw-zone for staging COPY input
Administrator access to the whole Redshift Serverless workgroup
questions.explain: It's the narrowest role in the pipeline — read-only, and scoped only to the curated zone bucket the COPY command reads from.

questions.q: What is the practical benefit of least-privilege IAM roles if one role's credentials are ever compromised?
options: The blast radius stays limited to whatever that one narrow role can do, not the whole account
Compromised credentials become impossible to use at all
AWS automatically revokes compromised credentials within seconds
It has no practical security benefit, only compliance value
questions.explain: Least privilege limits blast radius — a compromised northfield-redshift-copy-role, for example, can only read one bucket, not touch the whole pipeline.

questions.q: What is the common shortcut this lesson explicitly warns against?
options: Granting 'Resource': '*' for an action instead of naming the specific resource ARNs a role actually needs
Using IAM roles at all instead of hardcoded access keys
Creating more than three IAM roles for one pipeline
Using JSON instead of YAML for policy documents
questions.explain: The guide calls out 'Resource: *' as a shortcut that silently widens a role's power as the account grows, versus scoping to exact ARNs.
